# freight-audit-lab

By [Your name] · Live dashboard: [dashboard link] · Synthetic data only; every dollar figure is an estimate.

A simulated freight invoice audit and month-end accrual pipeline. It generates {{scale.shipments|int}} shipments and {{scale.invoices_received|int}} invoices from {{scale.carriers}} invented carriers, seeds them with billing errors and traps (invoices that look wrong but are not), audits them, and accrues unbilled freight each month-end.

## The comparison

The baseline is a careful spreadsheet pass, not a strawman: same rules, tolerances and fuel check, and it strips BOL formatting. It lacks context: rate effective dates, reweigh certificates, authorization timing, and which invoices a rebill replaced.

| | Precision | Recall | False flags |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Engine | {{engine_vs_baseline.overall.engine.precision|pct}} | {{engine_vs_baseline.overall.engine.recall|pct}} | {{engine_vs_baseline.overall.engine.fp|int}} |
| Careful baseline | {{engine_vs_baseline.overall.baseline.precision|pct}} | {{engine_vs_baseline.overall.baseline.recall|pct}} | {{engine_vs_baseline.overall.baseline.fp|int}} |

Recall is nearly the same; precision is not. A false flag is a dispute the carrier rejects: wasted analyst time and goodwill. Its {{baseline_fp_causes.total|int}} false flags each have one cause: rate amendments {{baseline_fp_causes.causes.rate_amendment.false_flags|int}}, late authorizations {{baseline_fp_causes.causes.late_authorization.false_flags|int}}, reweigh certificates {{baseline_fp_causes.causes.reweigh.false_flags|int}}, rebills and balance-due invoices {{baseline_fp_causes.causes.rebill_balance_due.false_flags|int}}, weight errors also flagged as rate errors {{baseline_fp_causes.causes.weight_misread_as_rate.false_flags|int}}, BOL typos or dropped zeros {{baseline_fp_causes.causes.bol_typo_or_zero.false_flags|int}}, other {{baseline_fp_causes.causes.other.false_flags|int}}. Missing context, not string cleaning.

## Read the engine's numbers with care

Near-perfect engine precision is expected: I built the generator and the engine, so the engine knows the rules of the world it is tested on. It shows the logic is coherent, not that it would survive real invoices. The useful results are four:

1. **Where the baseline fails.** Its duplicate flags were {{baseline_duplicates.false_share|pct0}} wrong ({{baseline_duplicates.false_flags|int}} of {{baseline_duplicates.flags|int}}), {{baseline_duplicates.share_explained_by_rebills_and_balance_due|pct0}} of the wrong ones from rebills and balance-due invoices, which legitimately repeat an invoice's BOL.
2. **Where the engine misses.** It missed {{engine_misses.missed|int}} injected errors, {{engine_misses.below_tolerance|int}} of them below its own tolerances, worth {{engine_misses.missed_true_dollars|usd}} (answer-key dollars). The sweep recommends changing {{recommended_tolerances.changed}} of {{recommended_tolerances.swept}} tolerances.
3. **The systemic-issue test.** {{systemic.strongest.carrier_name}} was flagged on {{systemic.strongest.flagged|int}} of {{systemic.strongest.invoices|int}} fuel surcharges shipped {{systemic.strongest.window_start|month}} to {{systemic.strongest.window_end|month}}, against {{systemic.strongest.other_carriers_rate|pct}} at the other truckload carriers (p = {{systemic.strongest.p_value|p}}). Each overcharge is only about {{systemic.strongest.mean_flag_dollars_estimate|usd}} (estimate), so the pattern, not any one invoice, is the finding. The test also flagged {{systemic.n_others}} weaker pattern (a high-error carrier): triage, not proof.
4. **The accrual diagnosis.** Accruals landed {{accruals.net_error_pct_estimate|abspct2}} {{accruals.direction}} eventual payable (mean monthly error {{accruals.mape_pct_estimate|pct2}}, estimates). Accessorials were only {{accruals.accessorial_share_of_accrual|pct}} of accrued dollars but {{accruals.accessorial_share_of_net_error|pct0}} of the net {{accruals.gap_word}}, and {{accruals.late_authorization_share_of_net_error|pct0}} of it is authorizations recorded after month-end.

## Approach

Generator with traps, four messy carrier layouts, normalization and matching, re-rating against the contract, rules, scoring against a sealed answer key, month-end accruals. Audit and accrual code never read the answer key (a test enforces it); an accrual at month-end M uses only what was known at M.

## Limitations

- Synthetic data. Error rates were injected, so the recoverable estimate ({{recoverable.total_estimate|usd}}, {{recoverable.pct_of_billed_estimate|pct2}} of billed) is circular. It is not a finding.
- Invented formats, no undercharges, no in-transit accruals, no scale noise (so the weight tolerance cannot be calibrated).
- The engine's {{engine_misses.engine_false_positives}} false flag is a typo'd BOL that matched no shipment. A person would clear it; it is left in.

## With real data I would

Ingest EDI 210 and PDF invoices, calibrate tolerances on dispute outcomes, use carrier-specific fuel tables, add undercharge liability, and learn which flags carriers accept.

## Run it

```bash
pip install -r requirements.txt
python -m freight_audit_lab.run
streamlit run streamlit_app.py
```
